edition.locus: Documenta Catholica Omnia Canones GR (sources/canones_GR.pdf), pp. 2-3, Canon ια´

source_text: Ἡ πρόσκλαυσις ἔξω τῆς πύλης τοῦ εὐκτηρίου ἐστίν, ἔνθα ἑστῶτα τὸν ἁμαρτόντα, χρὴ τῶν εἰσιόντων δεῖσθαι πιστῶν, ὑπὲρ αὐτοῦ εὔχεσθαι. Ἡ ἀκρόασις ἔνδοθι τῆς πύλης ἐν τῷ νάρθηκι, ἔνθα ἑστάναι χρὴ τὸν ἡμαρτηκότα ἕως τῶν κατηχουμένων, καὶ ἐντεῦθεν ἐξέρχεσθαι, ἀκούων γάρ, φησί, τῶν Γραφῶν καὶ τῆς διδασκαλίας, ἐκβαλλέσθω καὶ μὴ ἀξιούσθω προσευχῆς. Ἡ δὲ ὑπόπτωσις, ἵνα ἔσωθεν τῆς πύλης τοῦ ναοῦ ἱστάμενος, μετὰ τῶν κατηχουμένων ἐξέρχηται· ἡ σύστασις ἵνα συνίσταται τοῖς πιστοῖς καὶ μὴ ἐξέρχηται μετὰ τῶν κατηχουμένων. Τελευταῖον, ἡ μέθεξις τῶν ἁγιασμάτων.
orientation: A description, probably added to the letter later, of the stages of public penance, from weeping outside the church to sharing in the holy things.
pass_a_gloss: The weeping is outside the gate of the house of prayer, where standing, the one who sinned must beg the faithful going in to pray for him. The hearing [is] within the gate in the narthex, where the one who has sinned must stand until the catechumens, and from there go out; for hearing, it says, the Scriptures and the teaching, let him be cast out and not be counted worthy of prayer. The falling-under [is] that, standing inside the gate of the temple, he go out with the catechumens; the standing-together that he stand together with the faithful and not go out with the catechumens. Last, the partaking of the holy things.

choices.why: Plain English names of the four grades; ὑπόπτωσις is literally 'falling down'.
The dismissal of the catechumens is understood.
The main hall, as against the narthex.

pass_b_english: Weeping takes place outside the gate of the house of prayer. There the sinner must stand and beg the faithful who are going in to pray for him. Hearing takes place inside the gate, in the narthex. There the one who has sinned must stand until the catechumens leave, and go out from there; for, it says, “When he has heard the Scriptures and the teaching, let him be put out, and let him not be admitted to prayer.” Kneeling means that he stands inside the door of the church itself and goes out with the catechumens. Standing together means that he stands with the faithful and does not go out with the catechumens. Last comes sharing in the holy things.
notes: Rubric left out (editorial). Usually judged a later addition, not Gregory's own words: Vossius notes it was absent from the Greek Nomocanon and found only in Cardinal Sirleto's manuscript; translated in full as printed. Names of the grades: πρόσκλαυσις 'Weeping', ἀκρόασις 'Hearing', ὑπόπτωσις 'Kneeling' (literally falling down), σύστασις 'Standing together', μέθεξις τῶν ἁγιασμάτων 'sharing in the holy things'. ἕως τῶν κατηχουμένων ('until the catechumens') rendered 'until the catechumens leave' (the dismissal is understood). ναός rendered 'the church itself' (the main hall, as against the narthex). The quoted line (ἀκούων γάρ, φησί …) is not Scripture and its source is unnamed; left uncited. συνίσταται after ἵνα (indicative, late usage) kept and rendered as 'stands with'. Corrections χρἠ → χρὴ and μετᾶ → μετὰ follow the source note.
